title: Video Generation — Temporal Coherence with Joint Diffusion

questions.question: What does patchify_with_pos return for the toy video with T_FRAMES=6 and POS_DIM=4?
options: One vector of length 30 with all frames already flattened
Four vectors of length 6, with no position information
Six vectors of length 5: one frame value plus four position features
Six scalar values with the position discarded
questions.explanation: Each frame becomes `[video[t]] + sin_embed(t, POS_DIM)`, giving one value plus four positional coordinates.

questions.question: What is the flattened input width x_flat in train_joint?
options: 6 values because patchify removes position
6+4+8=18 values including only one frame
48 values because every frame gets a separate 8-dimensional timestep vector
6*(1+4)=30 values before the 8-dimensional diffusion timestep embedding
questions.explanation: flatten concatenates six length-5 frame-position vectors; the separate t_emb is appended later in forward.

questions.question: What does the joint denoiser predict for one noisy video clip?
options: A six-element noise vector, one epsilon estimate per frame
One scalar shared by all six frames
A class label for the clip's motion direction
A new positional embedding with four values per frame
questions.explanation: main initializes the network with out_dim=T_FRAMES, and train_joint compares its output to `eps`, a six-element noise vector.

questions.question: Why are time positions included in each patch before the joint forward pass?
options: They force every frame to have a different noise variance
They let the model distinguish the same numeric frame value at different temporal locations
They replace the diffusion timestep t entirely
They make the output vocabulary equal to T_FRAMES
questions.explanation: patchify_with_pos adds sin_embed(t, POS_DIM) for each frame index, providing temporal identity alongside the frame value.

questions.question: What length does frame_deltas(video) return for a six-frame clip?
options: One mean delta for the entire clip
Six differences including a wrap from the last frame to the first
Five absolute differences between consecutive frames
Thirty differences because positions are flattened
questions.explanation: The list comprehension iterates i over range(len(video)-1) and computes abs(video[i+1]-video[i]), yielding 5 values.

questions.question: What is the purpose of independent_per_frame in the demo?
options: It estimates FID from the six frame positions
It is the trained model's deterministic sampler with fewer reverse steps
It reconstructs the same clip while preserving all frame deltas
It provides a flicker baseline by sampling each frame without a joint temporal denoiser
questions.explanation: The baseline returns independent random-walk-like values, which main compares with joint sampling using average frame-to-frame deltas.
